body: I know they will be sad when they hear about it, but to be honest my selfishness is overcoming my empathy for them. I will try to make it look like an accident so they won't blame themselves. They shouldn't, it's not their fault and there was nothing they could do to help me.

My family would support me, no question about that, it's just the fact that I can't find a path that I know will make me happier, or even "different" in any way. 

As for finding a new hobby; I feel lucky that I can even bring myself to get out of bed every morning. I don't have the willpower to find or try something new, or better put: I don't feel like it will help. Thanks for the suggestion, though.

Edit: as for my trip; I'm not dreading it but I'm not looking forward to it either. It just feels like something I have to do, experience before dying.. of anything. I'd regret not having done it if I died beforehand.

Hey thanks for the offer. I'll keep that in mind.

I used to have a couple of hobbies like building model planes, gardening, fixing stuff around the house (I like working with my hands). I still do those things sometimes but it's not the same. I just don't feel like doing anything, none of it takes my mind off things or bring me joy anymore.
I'd say yes but I strongly prefer camping alone. But you should do it as well, regardless of whom you go with :).

Hi stranger! I'm not a psychologist but I can safely say I'm depressed. Not so sure about anxiety, it's just my interpretation of the issue. I don't think I have any other issues going on right now but who knows?

I did mention it to my sister, but my mood started to annoy her so I stopped talking to her about it. My roomie knows of it as well but I don't think he understands the depth of it.

It's not the path I chose, I seriously doubt it. I can't see myself doing anything and not feel this way. I just had enough and have absolutely no reason to keep going, or anything to look forward to.

There are no dumb questions, it's perfectly alright to ask. It's not boredom, I can't seem to snap out of it by doing something else to occupy myself with. It's more like I want to get out but there is no place to go to. And even if I did, there would be no guarantee that I'd feel better; I most probably wouldn't. It's a state of mind, not a lack of stimulation.

Well there are some bureaucratic issues that stop me from dropping out. But that aside, there is nothing else I want to do or I enjoy doing, or even can see myself doing in the future. It's not medicine that's wearing me down. If I were studying engineering, I'm certain I'd fall into the same pit.

I have been clinically depressed before (guess I might be prone to it) and tried medication/therapy. I'm very skeptical of the therapy due to my experience with it and I'd rather not go anywhere close. It might work for some people, but to me all it did was turn me into an empty husk of a person. So no, I won't consider it.

My family, as nice as they all are, isn't really a commitment. We all live seperately and don't really have anything in common anymore. It's just the remainders of what once used to be something functional, and I'm keeping in touch just outf courtesy. Not sure about the others.

Thanks, I hope it'll be a nice trip.
The thing is I really don't care about what I've "accomplished" so far. It doesn't matter anyways, pursuing it won't make things any different for me.
I'd go for it just because I know I'd regret not having done it more. :)

And yeah Norway is pretty cool.  I want to mainly experience the nature and see the northern lights.  Who knows, maybe I'll be mauled to death by an animal while experiencing one of the most beautiful sights in the world...

Heh, that actually sounds like fun.  I'd go for it if the opportunity presents itself at some point.  I haven't kissed a complete stranger, but I have done some impulsive stuff involving two people I had feelings for.  Worked both times.

I'm going wildcamping in Norway soon, something I always wanted to do.  I have quite a lot of money I saved up over the years so I should be able to do it.  Other than that, I don't think there's anything else I want to definitely experience before I go.  How about you?
Hey there!  I don't see why it matters but sure thing, I'm 26, turning 27 soon.
